title: beads never export issues.jsonl — the ledger is invisible to git
description: psymail-mini syncs its ledger by committing .beads/issues.jsonl alongside code; its origin has no refs/dolt/data, so git IS the transport. CCP has no issues.jsonl at all: .beads/config.yaml lacks the 'export: auto: true' block (and sync.remote), so bd never writes the export and every bead filed here is invisible to git and lives only in the local embedded Dolt DB. Root cause is upstream in harness-starter — commands/add.sh runs 'bd init' and stops, and bd's default config ships the export block commented out ('Disabled by default'). psymail-mini's config was hand-edited 3 minutes after its bd init (Aug 10 19:10 -> 19:13); that hand edit is the step the harness extraction never captured.
acceptance_criteria: '.beads/issues.jsonl' exists, is tracked by git, regenerates on bd mutations, and contains the beads filed this session.
close_reason: Added 'sync.remote' + 'export: auto: true' to .beads/config.yaml and generated a clean full .beads/issues.jsonl (37 issues), now tracked in git as of 120a1de. Verified: the export contains this session's beads (ccp-kcc, ccp-459, ccp-v64, ccp-ait, ccp-e2e) and is not gitignored; scripts/verify.sh passed. Root cause is upstream in harness-starter, filed there as har-nqi (P0) with har-xoq/har-638/har-sul. Caveat carried in har-xoq: bd export is incremental and does not drop deleted issues — a full regen (rm issues.jsonl export-state.json && bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl) is the only reliably correct form.

title: README links upstream's docs as CCP's — security reports misroute to Vorssaint
description: The README rewrite (e9cddfb) presents SUPPORT.md, SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and CHANGELOG.md as CCP's docs, but all four are still upstream's, untouched by the fork. SECURITY.md sends vulnerability reports to vorssaintapp/vorssaint-utils/security/advisories/new, so a CCP security report lands in the upstream maintainer's private advisories. SUPPORT.md points bug reports at upstream's issue tracker. CONTRIBUTING.md is titled 'Contributing to Vorssaint' and describes upstream's layout, yet README cites it twice as covering CCP's layout and conventions. CHANGELOG.md is entirely Vorssaint releases with no CCP entries.
design: Rewrite SECURITY.md and SUPPORT.md as CCP's (real consequence, and conflicts on upstream merge are rare and cheap). Do NOT overwrite CONTRIBUTING.md or CHANGELOG.md — they are upstream files that keep receiving upstream commits, and overwriting them makes 'merge upstream/main' expensive, which the fork strategy depends on staying cheap. Relabel those two in the README as upstream's instead.
acceptance_criteria: No README link presents an upstream-authored doc as CCP's own. CCP has its own SUPPORT.md and SECURITY.md routing to bubblesunyum/control-center-pro. Docs that stay upstream's are labelled as upstream's.
close_reason: Rewrote SECURITY.md and SUPPORT.md as CCP's own; security advisories now route to bubblesunyum/control-center-pro with an explicit split for vendored upstream sources. README no longer presents CONTRIBUTING.md/CHANGELOG.md as CCP's — labelled as vendored upstream rather than forked, to keep 'merge upstream/main' cheap. Reviewed by reviewer-taste and reviewer-correctness (both clean, all links and claims verified against the repo); scripts/verify.sh passed. Committed 3d28645.

title: activate/deactivate lifecycle and idle CPU
description: Sampling runs only while the panel is visible, except for widgets that explicitly opt into background sampling for a menu-bar stat. Enforced through activate()/deactivate(). Engine work off the main thread, models publish on main.
acceptance_criteria: With the panel closed the app measures ~0% CPU over a minute; opening and closing repeatedly does not stack observers or timers; verified with a widget that actually samples.
close_reason: PanelArrangement owns the live widgets and starts/stops them with the panel; activation is idempotent there and in the sampler. SystemStatsWidget actually samples (1Hz) so the claim is testable. Measured 0.00s of CPU over 60s with the panel closed. The background-sampling opt-in from the description is NOT built — nothing needs it until the first menu-bar stat; see ccp-lr7.11. Shipped in 3242849.

title: edit mode: wiggle, remove, and drag between lanes
description: Long-press or an Edit button enters edit mode. Widgets wiggle via a small repeating rotationEffect with a random per-item phase offset so they do not sync, show remove badges, and become draggable. Prefer a custom drag gesture plus matchedGeometryEffect over .draggable/.dropDestination, which feel clunky for grid reordering. Drop targets: any position in any lane, plus an empty trailing lane that appears as a target to create a new lane.
acceptance_criteria: Reorder within a lane, move between lanes, and create a new lane by dropping into the trailing slot; layout persists across a relaunch; wiggle phases are visibly unsynchronised.
notes: lr7.2 owns PanelLayout.normalized() (prunes empty lanes, floors at one). Mutation verbs live here, and each must end in a normalized() call — that is what keeps the invariant without lr7.2 shipping the verbs. The trailing empty drop lane is a render-time affordance and must never be persisted. Reordering has to index around .unavailable slots, which are real positions in the lane.
close_reason: Long press starts edit mode; per-card random period and head start for the wiggle; remove badges; live drag between and within lanes with the layout mutating under the finger. The new lane opens on the LEFT — the panel is right-pinned, so a trailing column shoves every card sideways mid-drag (built it trailing first and watched it). Verified by driving a synthetic CGEvent drag at the real window. Shipped in fb0038c.

title: lane layout with placeholder widgets
description: Vertical lanes stacking widget cards, driven by the layout model and rendering whatever the registry provides. Placeholder widgets only at this stage.
acceptance_criteria: Lanes render from a persisted layout across a relaunch; panel width grows with lane count and stops at the screen width.
notes: Also from lr7.2's review: JSONFileStore.load() returns whatever is in the file, un-normalized — the wiring here must call .normalized() on it before rendering. And see ccp-pr6 (duplicate ids in a lane) before ForEach-ing [LaneSlot].
close_reason: Launch loads layout.json through JSONFileStore, normalizes, resolves against the registry and writes back; ControlPanel renders [[LaneSlot]] and draws UnavailableWidgetCard for an id this build lacks. Verified by hand-editing the file with a duplicate, an empty lane and an unknown id and relaunching: dedup and lane-closing applied, the unknown widget drew as a card and survived the round trip. Panel clamps to the visible frame — the clipping that clamp causes is ccp-p6g, and the capture proving it is owed (display was locked). Shipped in 7959c69.

title: glass card design system
description: The CCPUI vocabulary every widget draws from: spacing scale, corner radii (continuous, ~16-20), thin-material card fill, 1px white-alpha stroke, shadow, type ramp, accent for active toggles. Matches macOS Control Center's language; borrows nothing from Vorssaint, whose design is trademarked.
acceptance_criteria: A widget can be built without a single hardcoded spacing, radius, or colour literal; looks right in light and dark and against a bright and a dark wallpaper.
close_reason: CCPUI design system: Space/Radius/Stroke/Layout in Dimensions.swift, a deliberately tiny Palette (semantic aliases over four white/black alphas; everything else is a system colour), GlassCard as the surface and WidgetCard as what a widget writes. A widget is buildable with no spacing, radius or colour literal.

title: panel dismissal: outside click and Esc
description:
Dismiss on outside click via a global NSEvent monitor, and on Esc. The event monitor must be removed when the panel closes — a leaked global monitor is the classic version of this bug.

Multi-display placement was split out to ccp-lr7.10 and deprioritised.
acceptance_criteria: Outside click and Esc both dismiss; opening and closing 20 times leaves exactly one monitor installed at most.
close_reason: Global mouse monitor for a click in another app, local key monitor for Esc; installed on show, removed on hide. Only the mouse watch is global so the status item's own click isn't seen twice. EventMonitors is a seam over NSEvent, so 'twenty opens and closes leave nothing installed' is a test. Shipped in 7ee672b.

title: status item and non-activating glass panel
description: NSStatusItem toggles an NSPanel: .nonactivatingPanel, level .popUpMenu, collectionBehavior [.canJoinAllSpaces, .fullScreenAuxiliary]. Real blur via NSVisualEffectView (.hudWindow or .popover, blendingMode .behindWindow) wrapped for SwiftUI. Anchored top-right of the screen holding the status item, width growing leftward with lane count up to full width. Pre-warm the window at launch.
acceptance_criteria: Panel opens under 100ms perceived; blur is the real thing behind the window, not a material fill; anchored top-right of the screen holding the status item, correct with the menu bar auto-hidden. Multi-display anchoring is ccp-lr7.10.
close_reason: Status item toggles a borderless non-activating NSPanel at .popUpMenu, canJoinAllSpaces, anchored top-right of visibleFrame (so an auto-hidden menu bar is not a special case). Window and SwiftUI graph built at launch and never torn down. Blur ended up per-card rather than per-panel at the user's direction: the window is transparent and each GlassCard carries its own behind-window NSVisualEffectView, because a panel-wide backdrop reads as a dark container and SwiftUI materials can't blur the desktop. Panel size comes from the hosting view's fittingSize.

title: layout model and persistence
description: [Lane] where Lane = [WidgetID], Codable, persisted as JSON in Application Support. Decoding must survive a stored layout naming a widget the registry no longer has, without discarding the rest of the arrangement.
acceptance_criteria: Layout round-trips through JSON; a layout referencing an unknown widget id decodes with that entry dropped and everything else intact; covered by tests.
close_reason: PanelLayout as plain lossless Codable data, normalized() for the empty-lane and one-lane-floor invariants, LaneSlot + WidgetRegistry.resolve preserving unknown ids as visible slots, and a generic JSONFileStore. 6 new tests; gate green

title: design the CCPWidget protocol and registry
description: Everything hangs off this, so it comes first. CCPWidget with a static WidgetDescriptor (id, title, icon, default size, required permissions), makeView(), activate()/deactivate(), optional settings and compact/expanded variants. Plus WidgetRegistry listing what is available.
acceptance_criteria: A placeholder widget can be declared, registered, and rendered with no change to any other file; unit tests cover registry lookup and descriptor defaults.
close_reason: CCPWidget + WidgetDescriptor + WidgetRegistry in CCPKit/Widgets. Registry is composed by the app rather than a self-assembling shared instance, so tests stand up fixture registries; re-registering an id replaces it in place so gallery order stays declaration order. WidgetSize is a named enum in CCPKit and the points live in CCPUI. 10 tests.

title: the shell: panel, lanes, edit mode

Two children left the epic rather than closing with it: ccp-lr7.10 (multi-display) needs a second physical display its own criteria insist on, and ccp-lmr now blocks on ccp-8ld.3 for a real control to photograph. Neither is waiting on the shell.

title: notifications and full disk access catch up slower than the re-read behind refresh
description:
`activate()` re-reads on the next main-queue turn, which is enough for the
fields the engine writes through a plain `DispatchQueue.main.async`:
accessibility, screen recording, camera, microphone.

Notifications and Full Disk Access do not settle that fast. Notifications wait
on `UNUserNotificationCenter.getNotificationSettings`, a round trip to a system
daemon; Full Disk Access is probed on a utility queue by listing protected
directories. Both can take tens of milliseconds, so the first frame after the
panel opens can show a stale value for them.

Harmless today: only accessibility and audioCapture gate a widget, and the
subscription corrects both of these when they land. It becomes visible the
moment a widget declares one of them in `WidgetDescriptor.permissions` — so
whoever wires the first such widget should read this first.

Found by the correctness review on ccp-ec8.

title: dashboard readyKids counts only direct children, nested epics undercount
Permissions updates buffers while panel is shut, leaks observation until next grant
description:
`PermissionsAdapter.deactivate()` cancels the watch Task, but a task suspended
on `for await` over an AsyncStream is not woken by cancellation — the loop
only reaches its `Task.isCancelled` check when the next value arrives. So the
stream never terminates, `onTermination` never fires, and the Combine
subscription to `Permissions.shared` outlives the closed panel until some
permission changes and wakes the loop.

Idle CPU with the panel shut is a stated feature, and this is an observation
running against it. The buffering is the same fault seen from the other side:
AsyncStream defaults to unbounded, so yields pile up with nobody reading.

Fixing this needs deterministic teardown, which means whoever calls
deactivate() must hold the thing being torn down — the adapter, not the shim.
That makes this and ccp-bn9 one change.
close_reason: adapter owns the subscription and cancels it synchronously in deactivate(); a shut panel now observes nothing

title: shim owns Combine->AsyncStream bridging that belongs in the adapter ccp-8ld.1 follow-up
description:
`SystemPermissions.updates` builds an AsyncStream over `objectWillChange`,
which is a paradigm conversion, not a restatement of a type. The bridge rule
(Sources/VorssaintBridge/README.md) says a shim may restate but not decide,
and the taste review on ccp-8ld.1 flagged this as the one place the rule was
being stretched.

The shim should re-export upstream's publisher as-is — that *is* a
restatement, since Combine is the engine's native shape — and the adapter
should own the conversion and the lifecycle.

Landing with ccp-ec8: that bug needs the adapter to hold the subscription, so
the relocation is the fix rather than a tidy-up alongside it.
close_reason: shim re-exports upstream's publisher as changes:; the Combine->async conversion and its lifecycle moved to the adapter

title: a panel taller or wider than the screen is cut off, not reflowed
notes: ControlPanelController.sizeFitting clamps the panel to the visible frame minus the inset, so a layout with more lanes than the display can hold has its leftmost lanes cut by the window edge (the panel is anchored top-right). Same for a lane taller than the screen. Fine as a guardrail — five 240pt lanes need a 1300pt-wide display — but the real answer is either a horizontal scroll inside the panel, a cap on lanes with the overflow refused at drop time in edit mode, or a smaller lane width on small displays. Decide before edit mode lets anyone build a layout that wide.
close_reason: Decided: cap, not scroll. Layout.laneCapacity(inWidth:) says how many lanes a display can show; edit mode refuses the drop that would exceed it rather than letting the arrangement grow off-screen. The existing sizeFitting clamp stays as the guardrail for a layout carried over from a wider display. A horizontal scroll was rejected — macOS Control Center never scrolls sideways and the panel is a control surface, not a document. Shipped in fb0038c.

title: a layout with the same widget id twice in one lane resolves to duplicate LaneSlot ids
notes: LaneSlot.id is the WidgetID, so a lane listing the same id twice yields two slots with equal ids and a SwiftUI ForEach over [LaneSlot] renders undefined. Raised by reviewer-correctness on ccp-lr7.2, which declined to file it on the grounds that no mutation logic exists yet — but the path does not need mutation: PanelLayout.load() will happily return {"lanes":[["stub","stub"]]} from a hand-edited or partially-mangled file, and lr7.6 will ForEach it. Recommendation: fold dedup (keep first occurrence) into PanelLayout.normalized(), which is already the invariant-maintainer that prunes empty lanes and floors at one lane — same place, same call sites, no new concept. NOT done in lr7.2 because normalized()'s contract was agreed with laurel as exactly those two invariants and widening it was not mine to decide unilaterally. Cheap; do it before lr7.6 renders anything.
close_reason: normalized() now places a widget at most once, first placement wins, across the whole layout — a lane emptied by the dedup closes up under the existing rule. Three tests in PanelLayoutTests. Shipped in 7959c69.

title: decide the layout save policy for edit mode: debounce and off-main
notes: lr7.7 saves the layout after every drag mutation. JSONFileStore.save() is synchronous blocking I/O, so a naive save-per-mutation writes the file on the main thread mid-animation. Raised as an async-API finding by reviewer-taste on ccp-lr7.2 and declined there: the store is Sendable and actor-agnostic on purpose, so a caller can move it off-main, and making load() async would stop applicationDidFinishLaunching from having lanes ready when it builds the panel. The real decision is a save policy — debounce the writes and put them off-main — and it belongs with the mutation verbs, not the store.
close_reason: LayoutAutosave: debounced 500ms, the write itself off-main, last layout wins, flushed synchronously when the panel closes or the app quits. Launch no longer writes the layout back at all — with every edit saved, a rewrite nobody asked for is a silent edit of the user's file. Shipped in fb0038c.

where no card is drawn, or treat a gutter click as an outside click.

verification the panel dismissed itself in the middle of a three-click burst
and the click responsible was never identified. Same surface, opposite
symptom — a gutter click doing nothing here, and something dismissing the
panel there — so treat them as one investigation into what the panel's
outside-click monitor considers inside. If they turn out to be independent,
split the phantom dismissal back out.

The panel never dismisses on a click that lands inside it, and a test or capture demonstrates the three-click burst that previously dismissed it leaving it open.

title: bd makes its own git commits, and they bypass the commit-msg hook
description:
Running 'bd dolt remote add' produced commit 815bc9b 'bd: update sync.remote' — authored as the user, not requested, touching .beads/config.yaml (it stripped the trailing newline, nothing more).

Two problems:
1. bd commits to git on its own. This repo's profile is conservative about git actions, and CLAUDE.md says not to commit without authority. A tool that commits as a side effect of a config read/write breaks that expectation silently.
2. The message names no bead. scripts/hooks/commit-msg would reject 'bd: update sync.remote' — the regex needs a ccp- id — so bd is committing with the hook bypassed. That is the same drift ccp-jze was filed for, except the bypass is not a human typing --no-verify, it is a tool doing it invisibly.

Nothing was harmed here; the commit is a one-character whitespace change. The concern is the mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: Either bd's self-commits are disabled, or the hook and the docs acknowledge that bd is a sanctioned committer and its commits are exempt by design rather than by accident.
notes: Found while wiring the Dolt transport (ccp-0t2). Same class of issue as ccp-jze, which removed the --no-verify advertisement from the hook.

title: the engine bridge, and the Permissions adapter
description:
Every upstream type is internal, and VorssaintEngines is a separate module, so
nothing in the engine layer is reachable from CCPKit today. This bead
establishes the seam that unblocks the whole widget epic, and adapts the one
piece of shared infra v1 actually needs.

Sources/VorssaintBridge/ is compiled into the VorssaintEngines module
(sources: ["Vorssaint", "VorssaintBridge"]), so its files are module-mates of
upstream and can re-export internal types as public. It holds visibility shims
ONLY — no branch, no stored property, no decision. Anything that decides
belongs in a CCPKit adapter.

Originally scoped as "port seven files". Six of the seven turned out not to be
v1 work, and the survey is recorded on the bead rather than lost:

- BoundedProcessRunner needs no shim: its consumers (DiskSampler,
  PeripheralBatterySampler, NetworkProcessSupport, MaxCapacityProbe) are all
  inside the engines module. Transitive, invisible to CCP.
- Notifier has no v1 consumer — upstream UI/, WhatsApp, updates, cleaner, and
  MonitorAlertService, which is ccp-mlw.
- HotkeyManager + GlobalShortcut: v1's definition of done has no global
  hotkey. Deferred to its own bead.
- LaunchAtLogin: unblocked (L10n is in Core/, not on the exclude list) but not
  in the definition of done. Its own bead.
- Defaults: shim individual DefaultsKey entries on demand as adapted engines
  need them, rather than porting 1730 lines of upstream preference surface.
acceptance_criteria: Sources/VorssaintBridge/ compiles into VorssaintEngines and re-exports what CCPKit needs; CCPUI imports no upstream type. A permission can be queried through a CCPKit adapter and its denial rendered as the panel's inline degraded state, unit-tested against a fake permission source across granted/denied/undetermined.
close_reason: VorssaintBridge compiled into VorssaintEngines as module mates, re-exporting Permissions as public PermissionSnapshot/PermissionKind/PermissionAuthorization and SystemPermissions. CCPKit's PermissionSource/PermissionsAdapter sits on the seam, mapping WidgetPermission to PermissionKind, exposing PermissionState and unmet set for inline grant, with activate/deactivate lifecycle that refreshes and watches via MainActor-isolated task. Deferred yield fixes stale objectWillChange read, nonisolated watch fixes deinit isolation, Equatable added, Package manifest silences 34 unhandled-file warnings by excluding CCP siblings. Unit-tested against FakePermissionSource across granted/denied/undetermined/indeterminate, activate idempotence, grant while open, and deactivate stops watching. Follow-ups filed as ccp-bn9 (shim bridging belongs in adapter), ccp-ec8 (buffer while shut), ccp-5xe (nested epic miscount). ccp-78w and ccp-c2m split out as hotkey and launch-at-login.

title: widget gallery for adding widgets
description: The + affordance in edit mode opens a gallery built from WidgetRegistry, showing each descriptor and whether its permissions are satisfied.
acceptance_criteria: Adding from the gallery places the widget and persists; already-placed widgets are indicated; gallery needs no change when a new widget is registered.
notes: Correction to the close reason: the follow-up commit is 9ed791f, not 4a3f2c1 — I wrote the hash before making the commit.
close_reason: The + in the editing bar opens a popover built from the registry: every widget the build offers, checkmarks on the placed ones, and the permissions a widget will ask for (sorted — the set has no order). Adding drops it into the shortest lane. Verified in the app end to end: removed the audio mixer, watched it leave layout.json, added it back from the gallery, watched it return. Registering a widget remains the whole of adding it to the gallery. Whether a permission is *granted* is ccp-23w. Shipped in 17ae630 and 4a3f2c1.

title: revisit graphify integration - keep or remove
description:
Graphify was spiked on 2026-09-01 (code-only AST, 14,770 nodes / 40,672 edges, 5x token reduction on avg query, 2.3-17.8x per question). Installed as on-demand skill at .claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md (no always-on hook, no committed graphify-out/) to keep always-loaded cost at 4105 tokens.

Check in after ~2 weeks of real use:
- Are queries actually replacing 2+ file reads per lookup? Check opencode-stats-for-nerds / manual.
- Is the scoped corpus (CCPKit/CCPUI/ControlCenterPro) useful, or do we need to include selected Vorssaint dirs?
- Are duplicate-ID warnings or community noise bothering queries?
- Does the .graphifyignore need tuning?

Removal / turn-off instructions (complete, no step leaves a residue):
1. Remove the skill (the only harness-visible piece):
   rm -rf .claude/skills/graphify
2. Remove the graph + ignore:
   rm -rf graphify-out/ Sources/graphify-out/ .graphifyignore
   # also clear any per-subdir extracts if you ran them:
   rm -rf .claude/skills/graphify/graphify-out 2>/dev/null; true
3. Remove hooks if you ever added them (spike did not, but full install would have):
   graphify hook uninstall  # or: uvx --from graphifyy graphify hook uninstall
   git config --unset merge.graphify.driver 2>/dev/null; true
   rm -f .git/hooks/post-commit .git/hooks/post-checkout 2>/dev/null; true
   # verify: graphify hook status  /  bd memories check
4. Clean gitignore entry if you added one:
   Edit .gitignore and remove the 'graphify-out/' line in the CCP block (if present).
5. Remove the Python tool if installed isolated:
   uv tool uninstall graphifyy 2>/dev/null; pipx uninstall graphifyy 2>/dev/null; true
   # if you only used uvx --from graphifyy, nothing to uninstall.
6. Bless the harness (removing the skill changes tracked docs):
   scripts/context.py bless
   scripts/verify.sh --quick  # should still pass
7. Close this bead:
   bd close ccp-4q8 --reason 'kept|removed because ...'

title: follow-up: design-system token polish for toggles (animation token, spacing collapse)
multi-display placement: open on the display holding the status item
description:
Split out of ccp-lr7.4, which now covers dismissal only. The panel should appear on the display holding the status item (or, failing that, the one under the mouse), and anchor correctly there — including with the menu bar auto-hidden and with displays of differing scale factors.

Deprioritised deliberately: single-display placement is what the shell is being designed and reviewed against for now, and the multi-display case needs hardware to verify honestly rather than reasoning about NSScreen.
acceptance_criteria: With two displays attached, the panel opens top-right of the screen holding the status item and is anchored correctly there; verified on real hardware, not asserted from NSScreen arithmetic.
notes: Moved out of ccp-lr7 when that epic closed. Not abandoned and not blocked on any code: its own acceptance criteria refuse an NSScreen-arithmetic argument and demand a second physical display, which no session has had. Everything it touches is one method, ControlPanelController.show(from:), which already asks the status item for its screen and falls back to NSScreen.main — so this is a verification task with a small fix behind it, not a build.

title: revisit the 38-file exclude list once the shell is real
description: The exclude list in Package.swift was arrived at by iterating swift build until it went green — the second, third and fourth waves are files that fell out behind an earlier exclusion, not files with their own UI coupling. Once ccp-4kq.4 (the Permissions PR) or a similar routing lands, some of them may compile again without their blocker. Worth one pass: try removing the cascade entries and see which stick.
acceptance_criteria: every entry in the exclude list is there because that file itself names a UI type, not because something it depends on was excluded; or the ones that remain are documented as cascade.

title: smoke test for the --full gate
description: scripts/smoke.sh: launch the built app, assert the status item and panel came up, quit. verify.sh --full already calls it when present. This is the only check that can catch a shell that compiles and does not run.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/verify.sh --full runs it and fails when the app fails to launch.
